title: The Verb of Dying Things
tagline: A poet flees the city's grid to join a mystic and a naturalist in a decaying house, where the land itself is dreaming a new language.
themes: The Language of Wildness vs. The Grammar of Civilization
Animism and the Consciousness of Place
Decay as an Active, Creative Process
The Beat Search for Authenticity in a Non-Human World

chapters.title: The River That Flows Both Ways
The City's Ghost in the Posture
The Silence You Can Listen To

story: Write a chapter where Leo attempts to transcribe the 'language' of a specific natural feature (a stream, a rockface, a storm) into a poem, failing until he changes his method.
Create a journal entry from Mira's perspective, detailing her ritualistic observation of the copper beech's final days.
Write a dialogue where Arden explains the concept of 'ghosts in the soil'—not as spirits, but as historical traumas and joys imprinted on the land.
Draft a letter Leo writes back to someone in the city, trying and failing to explain what he is learning, the prose itself straining against urban logic.
technical: Build a 'Land-Dream Generator' that uses location data (topography, flora, weather history) to create symbolic, prose-poem descriptions of a place's consciousness.
Create a visual/textual piece contrasting 'The City as a Finished Sentence' (using grids, typography, stark geometry) with 'The Wilderness as a Verb' (using fluid, organic, process-based visuals).

council: Ursula K. Le Guin (descriptive anthropology of the unseen)
Arthur Rimbaud (systematic derangement of the senses & symbolic vision)

cover_prompt: A lone poet, his back to the viewer, walks away from a faint, geometric city grid etched in distant fog, towards a sprawling, decaying Victorian house where vines and wildflowers burst from the roof and windows, [Detailed Scene & Context: The house is a living entity; one wall is peeled back like bark to reveal glowing, pulsing root systems and crystalline fungi growing on the interior wallpaper, while a woman shaped from river clay and a man with a crown of antlers and pressed leaves observe from the overgrown porch], [Artistic Style & Medium: in the intricate, symbolic, and nature-infused style of Alfred Kubin and Arthur Rackham, rendered as a detailed pen and ink drawing with muted watercolor washes], [Composition & Camera: book cover framing, a centered and slightly low-angle composition that emphasizes the towering, dreaming house against a vast, swirling sky filled with cloud-forms that resemble archaic alphabets], [Lighting & Color Palette: dramatic chiaroscuro lighting with a single shaft of amber sunset light piercing the gloom, color palette of decaying greens, earthy umbers, bruised violets, and flashes of bioluminescent gold], [Quality & Technical Enforcers: masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, intricate details, professional composition, sharp focus, 8k resolution, flux dev].
